title: First Cyber Case
sensory_anchor: the screen that is not a room but is read like one, the cursor that blinks like a heartbeat, the glow that does not change pitch
emotional_signature: the tradecraft is the same. the tradecraft has always been the same. she just has a different door to kick now.
body: The task force office is on the third floor. The task force office is half Bureau, half Agency, and the half that is Agency makes the coffee worse. She is at a desk. The desk is not a desk she would have chosen three years ago. The desk is a desk that runs the same tradecraft through a different door. The screen is the room. The network is the building. The packet is the suspect. The [DIRECTOR] is in the office. The [DIRECTOR] says: same rules. Same chain of command. Same warrants. Same evidence chains. The only thing that changed is the terrain. She does not believe the [DIRECTOR] for the first week. She believes the [DIRECTOR] by the end of the first case. The first case is a regional hospital network. The first case is ransomware. The first case is the same case she would have run as a CT-Division field op, except the target is a server in a different country and the entry is an SSH credential that was phished from a nurse who clicked a link in an email that looked like a benefits portal. The tradecraft is the same. The tradecraft is: find the entry, trace the operator, build the case, arrest the operator. The tradecraft is: the threat is a person, the network is the room, the SSH credential is the door. She kicks the door. The door opens. The case is made. The [DIRECTOR] does not say: I told you so. The [DIRECTOR] says: the case file is in the right format. The format is the same. The format has always been the same. The format is what holds when the door is not a door.

title: Intrusion Investigation
sensory_anchor: the log entries that look like noise and the one entry that is not noise, the timestamp that is three minutes off from every other timestamp
emotional_signature: the network is a room. the room is read the way rooms are read. she has been reading rooms since she was seven.
body: The intrusion has been live for six weeks. The intrusion is in a defense contractor's research network. The intrusion is patient. The intrusion is the kind of patient that means state-sponsored. The analysts on the task force have been working the artifacts: IP addresses, malware signatures, command-and-control infrastructure. The artifacts are a wall. The artifacts are a wall she has seen before. The artifacts are a wall that is the symptom, not the disease. She asks for the operational logs. The operational logs are the timestamps. The timestamps are the room. She reads the room. The room says: the operator logs in at 14:37 local time. The operator logs out at 22:11. The operator does not log in on weekends. The operator does not log in on the contractor's holidays. The operator logs in on the operator's holidays. The operator is in a timezone that is nine hours ahead. The operator's public holidays are not the contractor's public holidays. The operator is in a country that is not the country the IP addresses say. The IP addresses are the decoy. The timestamps are the truth. The room told her. The room always tells her. The room has always told her. The room told her in the stepfather's house. The room told her in SEAL-006. The room tells her now in a log file from a defense contractor. The room does not care what door she is reading. The room is a room. She is the one who reads it. The attribution is in the timestamps. The attribution is nine hours and a holiday calendar away from the IP addresses. The task force moves. The [DIRECTOR] confirms. The case is now an Agency case. The Agency case is built on Bureau tradecraft. The tradecraft is the same. The tradecraft has always been the same.

title: Digital Forensics on Seized Device
sensory_anchor: the laptop in the evidence bag, the air-gap workstation, the password prompt that is a wall she has learned to read
emotional_signature: the device is the room. the device has been opened before. devices always have.
body: The laptop was seized in the raid. The raid was CT-Division, not cyber, but the laptop is hers. The laptop is hers because the forensic analyst on the team is on vacation and the analyst's backup is sick and the case cannot wait three days for the analyst to come back. The case cannot wait because the [DIRECTOR] has a court date. The [DIRECTOR] has a court date because the [DIRECTOR] works cases that have court dates. The laptop is in an evidence bag. The laptop is on the air-gap workstation. The air-gap workstation is in a room that has no network connection. The room is the only kind of room she has not read before. The room is a server room. The server room is read like a server room. The password prompt is a wall. The wall is read like a wall. The wall says: the user named the laptop after a pet. The pet's name is in the file metadata. The file metadata is a folder. The folder is on the desktop. The folder is named 'for recovery'. The folder is for the recovery of a password the user did not want to recover. The password recovers. The laptop opens. The laptop is the room. The laptop is read like a room. The laptop has: emails, browser history, a folder of cryptocurrency wallets, and a folder named 'do not open'. The folder named 'do not open' is opened. The folder contains the case file. The case file is on the laptop. The case file is in the evidence. The case file holds up in court. The case file holds up because the evidence chain is intact. The evidence chain is intact because she read the device like a room. The device is a room. Devices are rooms. She has been reading rooms since she was seven. She will read rooms until the rooms run out. The rooms do not run out. The rooms just change doors.

title: The Phishing Pattern
sensory_anchor: the email that is too well-written to be a person, the urgency that is the hook, the human at the other end of the click
emotional_signature: the operator is a person. persons are rooms. she reads the room even when the room is an inbox.
body: The phishing campaign is targeting the State Department. The phishing campaign is good. The phishing campaign is the kind of good that means a real operator wrote it. The operator wrote it in English. The English is not the operator's first language. The English is the operator's fourth or fifth language, because the idioms are not idioms, the idioms are translations, the translations are slightly off in a way that only a polyglot would notice and she is a polyglot because the grandmother did not raise children who only spoke one language. The operator is targeting mid-level officials. The operator is targeting people who have access but not clearance. The targeting is the targeting of someone who knows which doors are not locked. The targeting is the targeting of someone who has read the org chart. The operator has read the org chart. The operator has read the org chart the way she reads the org chart in CT-Division. The org chart is a room. The org chart says: this person is the soft spot. The soft spot is the human. The human is the door. The human is always the door. She tells the [DIRECTOR]: the operator has read the building. The [DIRECTOR] says: how do you know. She says: the building told me. The [DIRECTOR] does not ask what building. The [DIRECTOR] has been in the room when she reads rooms. The [DIRECTOR] has learned that the rooms are everywhere. The campaign is mapped. The campaign is mapped by the targeting pattern. The targeting pattern is a person. The person is in a country that is not the country the emails say. The person is the operator. The person is the case. The case is built on the pattern. The pattern is the room. The room is read. The door is opened. The person is the door. The person is always the door.
